title: Atlanta United 1-3 Inter Miami: Messi doubles up again
subtitle: Inter Miami surged to a 3-1 win over Atlanta United on Saturday, with Lionel Messi once again scoring twice.
paragraphs: Lionel Messi doubled up once more to lead Inter Miami to a 3-1 victory over Atlanta United.
Messi scored twice in Miami's 4-0 win over D.C. United last weekend, though he did not find the net in a 2-0 defeat of New York City FC in midweek.
However, Messi was back on target twice on Saturday as Miami eased to a triumph at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Messi had seen a free-kick kept out by Atlanta goalkeeper Lucas Hoyos before German Berterame put Miami up on the stroke of half-time, turning in from Luis Suarez's cross.
Miami's captain then put the contest to bed with two goals in the space of four second-half minutes.
First, Messi combined with Berterame before slotting home at the end of a brilliant run.
Then, the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner latched onto Suarez's pass, turned his marker inside out and duly finished.
Messi looked set to get the chance to score a hat-trick when Paulo Diaz was pinned for handball, though VAR intervened, deeming that Suarez had committed a foul first.
Matt Edwards struck the woodwork for Atlanta, though the hosts did get a consolation late on when Maximiliano Falcon felled Fafa Picault, who dispatched the resulting spot-kick.
More MLS history for magnificent Messi
Messi has now gone 12 straight regular-season matches with a goal involvement.
The only longer single-season streak in MLS history is 15, set by Josef Martinez in 2019, with Messi now matching Sebastian Giovinco's run of 12 games in 2018.
Messi has now scored 23 goals and set up 15 this season, making him the first player in MLS history to record at least 15 assists in three straight campaigns.
"I can't believe this guy does what he does at 39 years of age," Miami head coach Cristian "Kily" González said of Messi.
"And what makes me happiest is that he's happy. So if he's happy, he performs the way he performs, he enjoys... Every day that I see him, I smile.
"He's a player who never stops surprising you.
"To me, he's an alien. He's a player who amazes me in every action, during every training session that I watch. And God willing, he'll keep on amazing us until the day he decides to retire."
